correctness.rationale: For a one-way n-cycle CTMC with positive r_i, linear budget Σ_{i<n}r_i+q r_n≤B, stationary weights are π_i∝t_i=1/r_i; direct clockwise hitting times give K=e_2(t)/Σt. Fix two ordinary rates a,b with sum s; K as a function of v=1/a+1/b has strictly positive derivative [R²+H+2R/s]/[2(R+v)²], so averaging unequal equally priced rates strictly improves K. This proves unrestricted reduction to k=n−1 identical ordinary rates, not an assumed symmetry. With u=r_n/r_1, K=k(k+q u)((k−1)u+2)/(2B(ku+1)); derivative has sign q[k(k−1)u²+2(k−1)u+2]−k(k+1), increasing on u>0. Below q_c=k(k+1)/2 its unique root is the formula in RESULT.md and the sole global positive minimizer; at or above q_c, strictly increasing K gives unattained inf k²/B as u→0+, r_i→B/k. At q=1 the unique solution is uniform. SymPy differentiation and n=3,4 rational hitting-time checks are independent; 12516 saved tests alone are not proof.
